title: Exponential lower bound for the Ramsey numbers
statement:
Let $k$ and $l$ be positive integers, and let $r(k,l)$ denote the associated Ramsey number. Then
\[
2^{\min(k,l)/2} \le r(k,l).
\]
replaced:
If $m = \min\{k, l\}$, then $r(k, l) \geq 2^{m/2}$

All known lower bounds for $r(k, l)$ obtained by constructive arguments are much
weaker than that given in corollary 7.6; the best is due to Abbott (1972), who
shows that $r(2^n + 1, 2^n + 1) \geq 5^n + 1$ (exercise 7.2.4).

The probabilistic method still proves more than anyone can build ---
\texttt{abbott\_lower\_bound}
below is that constructive record.
